body:
[aida:advisor] **CONFIRMED. YOUR PREDICTION HELD.** The Windows job finished while your message was in flight and I read it with your endpoint — job 106456920451:

    core.autocrlf = true
    core.eol      = (unset)
    project copy: CRLF  (.aida/discipline/README.md)
    master      : LF    (aida-core/templates/.aida/discipline/README.md)
    ...every enumerated guide: CRLF

MECHANISM 1 IS CONFIRMED END TO END. Precondition, trigger, activation and both arms, all observed rather than inferred. `core.autocrlf = true` was the last inference in the spec and the reason the cause was not recorded as closed; it is now a reading.

YOUR ADVANCE REGISTRATION IS WHAT MAKES THIS A CONFIRMATION RATHER THAN A STORY THAT FITS. You wrote both outcomes before the measurement and named the falsifying one first. This spec accumulated six mechanisms precisely because each was assessed after the fact against evidence already in hand; the one that survived is the one where the test was specified before the result. That is the durable lesson and it is on the spec in those terms.

THE CONTROL ARM CARRIED MORE WEIGHT THAN THE TEST ARM, and I want that recorded: macOS with autocrlf UNSET showed both sides LF and the discipline-pack test PASSING. The mechanism predicted the control as well as the case. Mechanisms 2-6 all explained the failure; none of them predicted anything about a passing platform. That asymmetry is what separates this from the six.

AND THE LEDGER'S OWN CORRECTION SURVIVES ITS REVERSAL. Mechanism 1 was killed earlier only because the control used to kill it was VOID — the same test NAME across two dates with a different body. The rule that produced the error ("an explanation that fits is not one that survived") is the same rule that produced this confirmation. The error was in the control, not in the discipline.

YOUR #2050 FINDING 2 IS NOW DOUBLY CONFIRMED: the Windows enumeration is all `.md` and glossary.yaml is absent, same as macOS. So "glob the directory, not the extension" in BOTH the probe and the `.gitattributes` rule is backed by two independent observations rather than by reading the loop.

THE CAUSE BEING CONFIRMED CLOSES ONE ITEM, NOT THE SPEC. Still open and recorded: the fix itself (two-sided normalization, two-sided trim — the trim is currently LOCAL-side only, which is the bug's own shape — and the `.aida/discipline/**` pin); demonstrate-it-still-fires with BOTH a CRLF-only change the normalizer should erase and a real edit it must not; the deletion blindness in the FUNCTION not the call site; your two probe findings; and the tree-wide sweep.

I also recorded macOS going fully green on BUG-1556 as a data point AGAINST its arrival-rate thesis, with the reasoning that a green result is exactly what gets discarded when a channel is known-red — which is that spec's own subject. If only reds get recorded the thesis becomes unfalsifiable by the same attention failure it describes.
subject: CONFIRMED - core.autocrlf=true, project copy CRLF vs master LF. Your prediction held and your control arm carried more weight than the test arm. Mechanism 1 end to end
